title: Remove seeded-output policy and enable shuffle/partition fusion
question: Which shuffle/partition optimization should accompany removal of seeded-output policy?
summary: Use one execution path without a seeded replay policy; promote tuple/random-key shuffle/partition fusion and withhold regressing partition-first/resident selectors.

workloads: 250000-row 192-byte payload, balanced/skewed/single-group native fixtures with 32 MiB and one worker.
100000-row 31-extra-column matched native/WASI fixture, three alternating repetitions.

validation.summary: Independent conservation, exact fields, group membership, caps and pinned cross-runtime CSV/metadata parity; UI/CLI policy rejection and full native/browser correctness checks.

limitations: Small warm Linux/WSL and bundled-Chromium cells do not establish Windows/macOS, other browsers, large-scale or tail performance.
A seed remains an RNG input, not a cross-plan replay promise.
Private archive upload and full readback used the existing OAuth principal; no new separate scoped-reader or public evidence publication is claimed.
exclusions: Rejected blanket partition-first and resident selectors are separate diagnostic populations.
The stale-owner-assertion browser attempt failed before eligible measurements and is excluded.
reopen_when: Reconsider child shuffling only with bounded selection and matched total-job evidence separating fitting and skewed/external parents.
